claim: Cre-dependent viral systems permit the manipulation of many neuron types.
source: While Cre-dependent viral systems permit the manipulation of many neuron types, some cell populations cannot be targeted by a single DNA recombinase.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: Some cell populations cannot be targeted by a single DNA recombinase.
source: While Cre-dependent viral systems permit the manipulation of many neuron types, some cell populations cannot be targeted by a single DNA recombinase.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: The combined use of Flp and Cre recombinases can overcome the limitation of targeting cell populations with a single DNA recombinase.
source: Although the combined use of Flp and Cre recombinases can overcome this limitation, insufficient recombinase activity can reduce the efficacy of existing Cre+Flp-dependent viral systems.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: Insufficient recombinase activity can reduce the efficacy of existing Cre+Flp-dependent viral systems.
source: Although the combined use of Flp and Cre recombinases can overcome this limitation, insufficient recombinase activity can reduce the efficacy of existing Cre+Flp-dependent viral systems.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the abstract.

claim: tTARGIT AAVs utilize a Flp-dependent tetracycline transactivator (tTA) 'Driver' AAV and a tetracycline response element-driven, Cre-dependent 'Payload' AAV to express the transgene of interest.
source: tTARGIT AAVs utilize a Flp-dependent tetracycline transactivator (tTA) 'Driver' AAV and a tetracycline response element-driven, Cre-dependent 'Payload' AAV to express the transgene of interest.
evidence: This describes the design of the tTARGIT system developed in this study.

claim: The tTARGIT system was employed in Slc17a6FlpO;LeprCre mice to manipulate LepRb neurons of the ventromedial hypothalamus (VMH; LepRbVMH neurons) while omitting neighboring LepRb populations.
source: We employed this system in Slc17a6FlpO;LeprCre mice to manipulate LepRb neurons of the ventromedial hypothalamus (VMH; LepRbVMH neurons) while omitting neighboring LepRb populations.
evidence: This describes the experimental application of the tTARGIT system.

claim: The circuitry of LepRbVMH neurons was defined using the tTARGIT system.
source: We defined the circuitry of LepRbVMH neurons and roles for these cells in the control of food intake and energy expenditure.
evidence: This is stated as a finding in the abstract.

claim: LepRbVMH neurons have roles in the control of food intake and energy expenditure.
source: We defined the circuitry of LepRbVMH neurons and roles for these cells in the control of food intake and energy expenditure.
evidence: This is stated as a finding in the abstract.

claim: The tTARGIT system mediates robust recombinase-sensitive transgene expression.
source: Thus, the tTARGIT system mediates robust recombinase-sensitive transgene expression, permitting the precise manipulation of previously intractable neural populations.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the abstract.

claim: The tTARGIT system permits the precise manipulation of previously intractable neural populations.
source: Thus, the tTARGIT system mediates robust recombinase-sensitive transgene expression, permitting the precise manipulation of previously intractable neural populations.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion in the abstract.

claim: Cre-dependent viral vectors permit the manipulation of genetically identified neural types when used together with Cre recombinase-expressing mice.
source: Together with Cre recombinase-expressing mice, the available suite of Cre-dependent viral vectors permits the manipulation of genetically identified neural types.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Cre-dependent viral vectors do not permit the study of subpopulations of cells expressing a particular Cre allele.
source: However, this approach neither permits the study of subpopulations of cells expressing a particular Cre allele (Hodge et al., 2019; Mickelsen et al., 2019) nor permits the study of Cre-expressing cells within a defined Central nervous system (CNS) site while excluding the Cre-expressing cells in closely apposed brain regions.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Cre-dependent viral vectors do not permit the study of Cre-expressing cells within a defined CNS site while excluding the Cre-expressing cells in closely apposed brain regions.
source: However, this approach neither permits the study of subpopulations of cells expressing a particular Cre allele (Hodge et al., 2019; Mickelsen et al., 2019) nor permits the study of Cre-expressing cells within a defined Central nervous system (CNS) site while excluding the Cre-expressing cells in closely apposed brain regions.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of existing approaches.

claim: Restricting transgene expression to cells that express two marker genes can overcome the challenge of targeting specific cell populations.
source: Restricting transgene expression to cells that express two marker genes can overcome this challenge (Luan and White, 2007).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Early attempts at restricting transgene expression to cells expressing two marker genes utilized gene-specific, Cre-sensitive transgene-expressing alleles in combination with Cre alleles driven by distinct genes.
source: Early attempts at this approach utilized gene-specific, Cre-sensitive transgene-expressing alleles in combination with Cre alleles driven by distinct genes (Chen et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Another solution for restricting transgene expression involves expressing two Cre fragments across different transgenes with distinct promoters, reconstituting active Cre only in cells that express both pieces.
source: Another solution involves expressing two Cre fragments across different transgenes with distinct promoters, reconstituting active Cre only in cells that express both pieces (Hirrlinger et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Approaches using gene-specific alleles and split-Cre systems generally involve substantial investments of time and resources, as they require generating and interbreeding multiple new gene- and experiment-specific alleles.
source: These approaches generally involve substantial investments of time and resources, however, as they require generating and interbreeding multiple new gene- and experiment-specific alleles.
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of existing approaches.

claim: Transgene expression can be directed to cell types defined by two marker genes through the use of recombinase-dependent alleles containing a ubiquitous promoter and tandem STOP cassettes that are each excised by distinct recombinases.
source: Transgene expression can also be directed to cell types defined by two marker genes through the use of recombinase-dependent alleles (often inserted into the Rosa26 Locus) containing a ubiquitous promoter and tandem STOP cassettes that are each excised by distinct recombinases (Daigle et al., 2018; Sciolino et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Neuroscience research often requires a higher degree of spatial specificity than afforded by intersectional genetic models.
source: Neuroscience research often requires a higher degree of spatial specificity than afforded by the intersectional genetic models outlined above.
evidence: This is stated as a motivation for developing viral approaches.

claim: Stereotaxic injections of recombinase-sensitive viral vectors can restrict transgene expression to a narrow anatomical region.
source: Stereotaxic injections of recombinase-sensitive viral vectors can restrict transgene expression to a narrow anatomical region.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: AAVs generally represent the preferred viral system for Cre-dependent transgene expression, given their minimal toxicity and the speed and ease of their generation.
source: Adeno-associated viruses (AAVs) generally represent the preferred viral system for Cre-dependent transgene expression, given their minimal toxicity and the speed and ease of their generation.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge.

claim: Developing AAVs sensitive to multiple recombinases has been challenging because of the limited AAV genome size, which precludes the use of multiple recombinase-sensitive STOP cassettes.
source: Developing AAVs sensitive to multiple recombinases has been challenging because of the limited AAV genome size, which precludes the use of multiple recombinase-sensitive STOP cassettes (Wu et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The INTRSECT system overcomes the AAV genome size limitation by utilizing a single AAV vector that flanks the transgene coding sequence with lox and FRT sites in such a way that combinatorial expression of Cre and Flp permits expression of a functional pre-mRNA that can then be spliced to produce a mature coding sequence.
source: The INTRSECT system overcomes this limitation by utilizing a single AAV vector that flanks the transgene coding sequence with lox and FRT sites in such a way that combinatorial expression of Cre and Flp permits expression of a functional pre-mRNA that can then be spliced to produce a mature coding sequence (Fenno et al., 2020; Fenno et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The multiple inversion and splicing steps involved in the INTRSECT system can limit transgene expression, perhaps due to the relatively poor recombinase activity of Flp (and even optimized FlpO).
source: The multiple inversion and splicing steps involved in this system can limit transgene expression, however, perhaps due to the relatively poor recombinase activity of Flp (and even optimized FlpO).
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of the INTRSECT system, with speculation about the cause.

claim: Generating INTRSECT viruses that express new transgenes requires a relatively complex and labor-intensive design and optimization process.
source: Furthermore, generating INTRSECT viruses that express new transgenes requires a relatively complex and labor-intensive design and optimization process (Fenno et al., 2020; Fenno et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: tTARGIT AAVs are composed of a Flp-dependent tetracycline transactivator (tTA) 'Driver' AAV and a tetracycline response element (TRE)-driven Cre-dependent 'Payload' AAV to express the transgene of interest.
source: Seeking a dual recombinase-activated AAV system to overcome these limitations and that could be modified quickly and easily, we generated tetracycline transactivator (tTA)-driven Recombinase-Guided Intersectional Targeting (tTARGIT) AAVs composed of a Flp-dependent tetracycline transactivator (tTA) 'Driver' AAV and a tetracycline response element (TRE)-driven Cre-dependent 'Payload' AAV to express the transgene of interest.
evidence: This describes the design of the tTARGIT system.

claim: LepRbVMH neurons modulate metabolic adaptations to obesogenic diets.
source: We applied tTARGIT AAVs to the study of ventromedial hypothalamic LepRb (VMH; LepRbVMH) neurons, which modulate metabolic adaptations to obesogenic diets (Bingham et al., 2008; Dhillon et al., 2006) but have proven difficult to study directly due to the density and proximity of neighboring LepRb populations.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: LepRbVMH neurons have proven difficult to study directly due to the density and proximity of neighboring LepRb populations.
source: We applied tTARGIT AAVs to the study of ventromedial hypothalamic LepRb (VMH; LepRbVMH) neurons, which modulate metabolic adaptations to obesogenic diets (Bingham et al., 2008; Dhillon et al., 2006) but have proven difficult to study directly due to the density and proximity of neighboring LepRb populations.
evidence: This is stated as a challenge in studying these neurons.

claim: tTARGIT AAVs together with LeprCre and Slc16a7FlpO allowed the study of LepRbVMH neurons and revealed a specific role for these neurons in suppressing food intake and increasing energy expenditure to promote weight loss.
source: Together with LeprCre and Slc16a7FlpO, tTARGIT AAVs allowed us to overcome these challenges and reveal a specific role for LepRbVMH neurons in suppressing food intake and increasing energy expenditure to promote weight loss.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the study.

claim: The density of LepRb neurons in the adjacent arcuate nucleus (ARC), dorsomedial hypothalamus, and lateral hypothalamic area complicated initial attempts to study LepRbVMH neurons using LeprCre mice and Cre-dependent vectors.
source: The density of LepRb neurons in the adjacent arcuate nucleus (ARC), dorsomedial hypothalamus, and lateral hypothalamic area complicated our initial attempts to study LepRbVMH neurons using LeprCre mice and Cre-dependent vectors; viruses targeted to the VMH spread to other nearby LeprCre neurons, confounding the interpretation of our results (data not shown).
evidence: This describes an experimental challenge encountered in the study.

claim: Viruses targeted to the VMH spread to other nearby LeprCre neurons, confounding the interpretation of results.
source: The density of LepRb neurons in the adjacent arcuate nucleus (ARC), dorsomedial hypothalamus, and lateral hypothalamic area complicated our initial attempts to study LepRbVMH neurons using LeprCre mice and Cre-dependent vectors; viruses targeted to the VMH spread to other nearby LeprCre neurons, confounding the interpretation of our results (data not shown).
evidence: This describes an experimental challenge encountered in the study.

claim: Slc17a6, encoding the vesicular glutamate transporter 2 (vGLUT2) protein, expression is largely restricted to LepRbVMH neurons and absent from most surrounding LepRb cells.
source: Because Slc17a6, encoding the vesicular glutamate transporter 2 (vGLUT2) protein, expression is largely restricted to LepRbVMH neurons and absent from most surrounding LepRb cells (Vong et al., 2011), we generated a Slc17a6FlpO strain and crossed it with LeprCre and a novel Flp- and Cre-dependent reporter (Rosa26RCFL-eGFP-L10a).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: A Slc17a6FlpO strain was generated.
source: Because Slc17a6, encoding the vesicular glutamate transporter 2 (vGLUT2) protein, expression is largely restricted to LepRbVMH neurons and absent from most surrounding LepRb cells (Vong et al., 2011), we generated a Slc17a6FlpO strain and crossed it with LeprCre and a novel Flp- and Cre-dependent reporter (Rosa26RCFL-eGFP-L10a).
evidence: This describes a mouse line generated in the study.

claim: A novel Flp- and Cre-dependent reporter (Rosa26RCFL-eGFP-L10a) was generated.
source: Because Slc17a6, encoding the vesicular glutamate transporter 2 (vGLUT2) protein, expression is largely restricted to LepRbVMH neurons and absent from most surrounding LepRb cells (Vong et al., 2011), we generated a Slc17a6FlpO strain and crossed it with LeprCre and a novel Flp- and Cre-dependent reporter (Rosa26RCFL-eGFP-L10a).
evidence: This describes a reporter line generated in the study.

claim: Reporter mice with Slc17a6FlpO, LeprCre, and Rosa26RCFL-eGFP-L10a identified Cre- and Flp-co-expressing LepRbSlc17a6 neurons elsewhere in the brain.
source: Although these reporter mice identified Cre- and Flp-co-expressing LepRbSlc17a6 neurons elsewhere in the brain, within the mediobasal hypothalamus this approach largely limited eGFP expression to VMH cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Within the mediobasal hypothalamus, the combination of Slc17a6FlpO, LeprCre, and Rosa26RCFL-eGFP-L10a largely limited eGFP expression to VMH cells.
source: Although these reporter mice identified Cre- and Flp-co-expressing LepRbSlc17a6 neurons elsewhere in the brain, within the mediobasal hypothalamus this approach largely limited eGFP expression to VMH cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: Injection of the INTRSECT AAV system into the VMH of Slc17a6FlpO;LeprCre mice resulted in detectable ChR2 expression in one or fewer cells per section.
source: We injected the INTRSECT AAV system (Fenno et al., 2014) into the VMH of Slc17a6FlpO;LeprCre mice in an attempt to express channelrhodopsin (ChR2) in LepRbVMH cells. However, this approach resulted in detectable ChR2 expression in one or fewer cells per section (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 2.

claim: The poor recombinase activity of Flp and the more moderate Flp and Cre expression mediated by Slc17a6FlpO and LeprCre, respectively, might limit INTRSECT-mediated transgene expression in LepRbVMH cells.
source: We surmised that while INTRSECT works well in systems with robust Flp and Cre activities, the poor recombinase activity of Flp and the more moderate Flp and Cre expression mediated by Slc17a6FlpO and LeprCre, respectively, might limit INTRSECT-mediated transgene expression in LepRbVMH cells.
evidence: This is stated as an inference from the experimental results.

claim: The tTARGIT system is based on a previously described inducible gene expression system based on recombinase-dependent expression of the tetracycline transactivator (tTA) in combination with a TRE-driven transgene-expressing allele.
source: We therefore set out to develop a more sensitive AAV system to drive Cre+Flp-dependent transgene expression, using as our framework a previously described inducible gene expression system based on recombinase-dependent expression of the tetracycline transactivator (tTA) in combination with a TRE-driven transgene-expressing allele (Chan et al., 2017; He et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: The Driver AAV (AAV-hSYN1-fDIO-tTA) utilizes Flp-dependent Double-Floxed Inverted Open reading frame (fDIO) cassette to Flp-dependently invert tTA, permitting its expression by a human synapsin I (hSYN1) promoter.
source: The Driver (AAV-hSYN1-fDIO-tTA) utilizes Flp-dependent Double-Floxed Inverted Open reading frame (fDIO) cassette (Fenno et al., 2014) to Flp-dependently invert tTA, permitting its expression by a human synapsin I (hSYN1) promoter.
evidence: This describes the design of the Driver AAV.

claim: The Driver AAV contains two tetracycline operators (TetO) to drive a positive feedback loop and increase tTA expression.
source: This virus also contains two tetracycline operators (TetO) to drive a positive feedback loop and increase tTA expression (Chan et al., 2017).
evidence: This describes the design of the Driver AAV, with citation to prior work.

claim: The Payload AAV mediates tTA/TRE-dependent transgene expression following its Cre-mediated inversion into the sense orientation.
source: The Payload AAV mediates tTA/TRE-dependent transgene expression following its Cre-mediated inversion into the sense orientation.
evidence: This describes the design of the Payload AAV.

claim: Only cells that contain both Flp and Cre recombinases express the transgene in the tTARGIT system.
source: Hence, only cells that contain both recombinases express the transgene (Figure 1a).
evidence: This describes the logic of the tTARGIT system, illustrated in Figure 1a.

claim: Tetracycline inhibits tTA-dependent gene expression.
source: Tetracycline inhibits tTA-dependent gene expression (Das et al., 2016), so this system mediates constitutive payload expression in target cells in the absence of tetracycline.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: The tTARGIT system mediates constitutive payload expression in target cells in the absence of tetracycline.
source: Tetracycline inhibits tTA-dependent gene expression (Das et al., 2016), so this system mediates constitutive payload expression in target cells in the absence of tetracycline.
evidence: This is stated as a property of the tTARGIT system.

claim: No TdT (DSRed-immunoreactivity) was detected in the VMH of wild-type mice co-injected with AAV-hSYN-fDIO-tTA and AAV-TRE-DIO-ChR2-TdT.
source: We detected no TdT (DSRed-immunoreactivity [IR]) in the VMH of wild-type or Slc17a6FlpO animals and minimal expression in LeprCre mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1c and Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: No TdT (DSRed-immunoreactivity) was detected in the VMH of Slc17a6FlpO mice co-injected with AAV-hSYN-fDIO-tTA and AAV-TRE-DIO-ChR2-TdT.
source: We detected no TdT (DSRed-immunoreactivity [IR]) in the VMH of wild-type or Slc17a6FlpO animals and minimal expression in LeprCre mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1c and Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: Minimal TdT expression was detected in the VMH of LeprCre mice co-injected with AAV-hSYN-fDIO-tTA and AAV-TRE-DIO-ChR2-TdT.
source: We detected no TdT (DSRed-immunoreactivity [IR]) in the VMH of wild-type or Slc17a6FlpO animals and minimal expression in LeprCre mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1c and Figure 1—figure supplement 3.

claim: The Driver+Payload combination mediated robust DSRed-IR in the VMH of Slc17a6FlpO;LeprCre mice.
source: In contrast, the Driver+Payload combination mediated robust DSRed-IR in the VMH of Slc17a6FlpO;LeprCre mice (Figure 1c); furthermore, VMH photostimulation in these mice promoted robust colocalization of DSRed- and FOS-IR, consistent with the ability of this system to activate transduced Flp+Cre-expressing cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1c.

claim: VMH photostimulation in Slc17a6FlpO;LeprCre mice injected with Driver+Payload AAVs promoted robust colocalization of DSRed- and FOS-IR.
source: In contrast, the Driver+Payload combination mediated robust DSRed-IR in the VMH of Slc17a6FlpO;LeprCre mice (Figure 1c); furthermore, VMH photostimulation in these mice promoted robust colocalization of DSRed- and FOS-IR, consistent with the ability of this system to activate transduced Flp+Cre-expressing cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: The colocalization of DSRed- and FOS-IR following photostimulation is consistent with the ability of the tTARGIT system to activate transduced Flp+Cre-expressing cells.
source: In contrast, the Driver+Payload combination mediated robust DSRed-IR in the VMH of Slc17a6FlpO;LeprCre mice (Figure 1c); furthermore, VMH photostimulation in these mice promoted robust colocalization of DSRed- and FOS-IR, consistent with the ability of this system to activate transduced Flp+Cre-expressing cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is stated as an interpretation of the data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 4.

claim: Injecting the Driver AAV alone into the VMH of Slc17a6FlpO;LeprCre animals produced minimal or no detectable DSRed-IR.
source: As expected, injecting either virus alone produced minimal or no detectable DSRed-IR, while co-injection of the two viruses yielded robust DSRed-IR (Figure 1e).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1e.

claim: Injecting the Payload AAV alone into the VMH of Slc17a6FlpO;LeprCre animals produced minimal or no detectable DSRed-IR.
source: As expected, injecting either virus alone produced minimal or no detectable DSRed-IR, while co-injection of the two viruses yielded robust DSRed-IR (Figure 1e).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1e.

claim: Co-injection of the Driver and Payload AAVs into the VMH of Slc17a6FlpO;LeprCre animals yielded robust DSRed-IR.
source: As expected, injecting either virus alone produced minimal or no detectable DSRed-IR, while co-injection of the two viruses yielded robust DSRed-IR (Figure 1e).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1e.

claim: Robust transgene expression by the tTARGIT system requires injection of both the Driver and Payload AAVs, as well as the presence of both Flp and Cre recombinases.
source: Thus, robust transgene expression by the tTARGIT system requires injection of both the Driver and Payload AAVs, as well as the presence of both Flp and Cre recombinases.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion from the experimental results.

claim: The tTARGIT approach can be modified from a Flp-ON/Cre-ON system to a Flp-ON/Cre-OFF system.
source: The tTARGIT approach can also be modified from a Flp-ON/Cre-ON system, requiring both Flp and Cre recombinases for payload expression, to a Flp-ON/Cre-OFF system, mediating transgene expression in all Flp-expressing cells that do not contain Cre (Figure 1—figure supplement 5; Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5 and Table 1.

claim: The Flp-ON/Cre-OFF system mediates transgene expression in all Flp-expressing cells that do not contain Cre.
source: The tTARGIT approach can also be modified from a Flp-ON/Cre-ON system, requiring both Flp and Cre recombinases for payload expression, to a Flp-ON/Cre-OFF system, mediating transgene expression in all Flp-expressing cells that do not contain Cre (Figure 1—figure supplement 5; Table 1).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5 and Table 1.

claim: Placing the payload transgene in the forward orientation within the DIO cassette permits tTA-driven transgene expression in all Flp-expressing cells that do not contain Cre because Cre inverts the Payload transgene into the antisense orientation.
source: Placing the payload transgene in the forward orientation within the DIO cassette permits tTA-driven transgene expression in all Flp-expressing cells that do not contain Cre because Cre inverts the Payload transgene into the antisense orientation.
evidence: This describes the logic of the Flp-ON/Cre-OFF system.

claim: The Flp-ON/Cre-OFF tTARGIT system drove hM3Dq-mCherry expression almost exclusively in cells that did not express the Cre-dependent GFP when tested in Slc17a6FlpO;LeprCre;Rosa26LSL-GFP-L10a animals.
source: As expected, this modified tTARGIT system drove hM3Dq-mCherry expression almost exclusively in cells that did not express the Cre-dependent GFP (Figure 1—figure supplement 5c).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 5c.

claim: 1-7% of mCherry cells in the Flp-ON/Cre-OFF system showed detectable GFP-IR.
source: We surmise the few GFP-IR neurons with detectable mCherry, constituting 1–7% of all mCherry cells, might result from the low Cre expression mediated by LeprCre (Patterson et al., 2011) and predict that the Flp-On, Cre-Off tTARGIT system should demonstrate complete Payload inactivation when used in conjunction with a more robustly expressing Cre allele or require longer incubation periods to fully inactivate the payload transgene.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the data.

claim: The few GFP-IR neurons with detectable mCherry in the Flp-ON/Cre-OFF system might result from the low Cre expression mediated by LeprCre.
source: We surmise the few GFP-IR neurons with detectable mCherry, constituting 1–7% of all mCherry cells, might result from the low Cre expression mediated by LeprCre (Patterson et al., 2011) and predict that the Flp-On, Cre-Off tTARGIT system should demonstrate complete Payload inactivation when used in conjunction with a more robustly expressing Cre allele or require longer incubation periods to fully inactivate the payload transgene.
evidence: This is stated as speculation about the cause of incomplete Cre-OFF inactivation, with citation to prior work.

claim: The Flp-On, Cre-Off tTARGIT system should demonstrate complete Payload inactivation when used in conjunction with a more robustly expressing Cre allele or require longer incubation periods to fully inactivate the payload transgene.
source: We surmise the few GFP-IR neurons with detectable mCherry, constituting 1–7% of all mCherry cells, might result from the low Cre expression mediated by LeprCre (Patterson et al., 2011) and predict that the Flp-On, Cre-Off tTARGIT system should demonstrate complete Payload inactivation when used in conjunction with a more robustly expressing Cre allele or require longer incubation periods to fully inactivate the payload transgene.
evidence: This is stated as a prediction based on the experimental results.

claim: Co-injection of the Driver AAV and AAV-TRE-DIO-GFP-2A-SynmRuby Payload virus into the VMH of Slc17a6FlpO;LeprCre mice promoted robust VMH-restricted GFP-IR.
source: Co-injection of this tTARGIT Payload AAV and the Driver virus into the VMH of Slc17a6FlpO;LeprCre mice promoted robust VMH-restricted GFP-IR (Figure 2b).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2b.

claim: mRuby detection (DSRed-IR) for the AAV-TRE-DIO-GFP-2A-SynmRuby virus was much lower than for GFP.
source: mRuby detection (DSRed-IR) for this virus was much lower than for GFP, however (data not shown); thus, we used GFP-IR to detect projections from LepRbVMH cells.
evidence: This is stated as an observation from the data.

claim: GFP-IR was used to detect projections from LepRbVMH cells.
source: mRuby detection (DSRed-IR) for this virus was much lower than for GFP, however (data not shown); thus, we used GFP-IR to detect projections from LepRbVMH cells.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used.

claim: LepRbVMH cells project to the periaqueductal gray, the arcuate, the periventricular thalamic nucleus, the periventricular hypothalamic nucleus, the bed nucleus of the stria terminalis, and the preoptic area.
source: Assessing the entire CNS for the presence of GFP-IR revealed terminals in the periaqueductal gray, the arcuate, the periventricular thalamic nucleus, the periventricular hypothalamic nucleus, the bed nucleus of the stria terminalis, and the preoptic area (Figure 2c,d).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2c,d.

claim: The projections of LepRbVMH cells are consistent with the known projections of the VMH.
source: These are consistent with the known projections of the VMH (Canteras et al., 1994; Meek et al., 2016; Zhang et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Ablating Lepr expression from the VMH (Nr5a1Cre-mediated) promotes obesity associated with decreased energy expenditure in high-fat-diet-fed animals.
source: Ablating Lepr expression from the VMH (Nr5a1Cre-mediated) promotes obesity associated with decreased energy expenditure in high-fat-diet-fed animals, suggesting a specific role for LepRb signaling in LepRbVMH cells in the control of energy balance via the dietary modulation of energy utilization (Bingham et al., 2008; Dhillon et al., 2006).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work.

claim: Ablating Lepr expression from the VMH suggests a specific role for LepRb signaling in LepRbVMH cells in the control of energy balance via the dietary modulation of energy utilization.
source: Ablating Lepr expression from the VMH (Nr5a1Cre-mediated) promotes obesity associated with decreased energy expenditure in high-fat-diet-fed animals, suggesting a specific role for LepRb signaling in LepRbVMH cells in the control of energy balance via the dietary modulation of energy utilization (Bingham et al., 2008; Dhillon et al., 2006).
evidence: This is stated as an inference from prior work, supported by citations.

claim: Co-injection of the Driver AAV and AAV-TRE-DIO-hM3Dq-mCherry Payload virus into the VMH of Slc17a6FlpO;LeprCre animals promoted robust VMH-restricted expression of functional hM3Dq-mCherry.
source: We co-injected the Driver AAV and this AAV-TRE-DIO-hM3Dq-mCherry Payload virus into the VMH of Slc17a6FlpO;LeprCre animals (LepRbVMH-Dq mice; Figure 3a). This approach promoted robust VMH-restricted expression of functional hM3Dq-mCherry as administration of the DREADD activator (Pei et al., 2008), clozapine-N-oxide (CNO), stimulated colocalization of FOS with DSRed-IR cells (Figure 3b–d).
